deep.reconstruction:
This page is the working draft of §1 of Riemann's published memoir 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines flüssigen gleichartigen Ellipsoides' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 9, 1861). It continues the setup of the previous page, where the body-axis coordinates are ξ=αx+βy+γz etc. (eq. 2 there) and the 'second' frame is given by ξ/a = α1 x0/a0 + β1 y0/b0 + γ1 z0/c0 etc. (eq. 5 there).

(1) Equations of motion along the principal axes. For an incompressible fluid of unit density, Euler's equations ẍ = ε∂V/∂x − ∂p/∂x etc. are projected onto the instantaneous principal axes of the ellipsoid:
 α ẍ + β ÿ + γ z̈ = ε ∂V/∂ξ − ∂p/∂ξ,
 α' ẍ + β' ÿ + γ' z̈ = ε ∂V/∂η − ∂p/∂η,
 α'' ẍ + β'' ÿ + γ'' z̈ = ε ∂V/∂ζ − ∂p/∂ζ.
Here V is the gravitational potential, p the pressure at (x,y,z) at time t, and ε the gravitational constant (the attraction of two unit masses at unit distance). The stated aim is to rewrite both sides in terms of ξ, η, ζ.

(2) Velocity components on the moving axes:
 ξ' = α ẋ + β ẏ + γ ż, η' = α' ẋ + β' ẏ + γ' ż, ζ' = α'' ẋ + β'' ẏ + γ'' ż.
Differentiating ξ = αx + βy + γz gives
 dξ/dt = α̇ x + β̇ y + γ̇ z + ξ'.
Next substitute the inverse transformation (x = αξ + α'η + α''ζ, etc.; the explicit step is mine).

Orthonormality (α²+β²+γ²=1, αα'+ββ'+γγ'=0, …) gives, on differentiation:
- αα̇+ββ̇+γγ̇ = 0, and similarly for the other rows;
- the mixed sums are antisymmetric, e.g. αα̇'+ββ̇'+γγ̇' = −(α'α̇+β'β̇+γ'γ̇).
The three independent mixed sums are named p, q, r, with r = α'α̇+β'β̇+γ'γ̇, −q = α''α̇+β''β̇+γ''γ̇ and p = α''α̇'+β''β̇'+γ''γ̇' (sign conventions mine, fixed by eq. 3). The same quantities for the frame (α1,β1,γ1) are named p1, q1, r1.

Hence the part of dξ/dt that comes from the motion of the axes is rη − qζ, and
 (3) ξ' = dξ/dt − rη + qζ,
 η' = rξ + dη/dt − pζ,
 ζ' = −qξ + pη + dζ/dt.

(4) The same procedure applied to (2) gives the accelerations along the axes:
 α ẍ + β ÿ + γ z̈ = dξ'/dt − rη' + qζ', and cyclically (only the first row is written).

(5) Applying the same differentiation to the previous page's (5), with x0, y0, z0 fixed:
 d(ξ/a)/dt = r1 η/b − q1 ζ/c,
 d(η/b)/dt = −r1 ξ/a + p1 ζ/c,
 d(ζ/c)/dt = q1 ξ/a − p1 η/b.

(6) Using dξ/dt = ȧ ξ/a + a·d(ξ/a)/dt etc. in (3):
 ξ' = ȧ ξ/a + (a r1 − b r) η/b + (c q − a q1) ζ/c,
 η' = (a r − b r1) ξ/a + ḃ η/b + (b p1 − c p) ζ/c.
The third row, which the page leaves unfinished, would be (mine):
 ζ' = (c q1 − a q) ξ/a + (b p − c p1) η/b + ċ ζ/c.

Interpretation, as Riemann states it:
- ξ', η', ζ' are the absolute velocity components parallel to the moving ξ, η, ζ axes;
- dξ/dt, dη/dt, dζ/dt are the velocities relative to that moving frame;
- the next page adds that p, q, r are the instantaneous angular velocities of the frame about its own axes.
The programme continues on the next page: insert (6) into (4) so the left sides become linear in ξ, η, ζ, then match coefficients with the right side, which is quadratic in ξ, η, ζ. This leads to the system for a, b, c, u, v, w, u', v', w'.
errors: No substantive mathematical errors on the page; every displayed relation checks out.
Riemann's sign convention (r = Σ α'α̇, −q = Σ α''α̇, p = Σ α''α̇') is left implicit. It is recoverable only from eq. (3).
Equations (1), (2) and (4) are written out only in their first row; the other rows and the third line of (6) are left blank.

The machine transcription's '+q1 ζ/c' in the first equation of (5) must be '−q1 ζ/c' to agree with the antisymmetric pattern of the other two equations and with (6). The image is ambiguous; see corrections.

results.what: Projection of Euler's hydrodynamic equations onto rotating principal axes, with accelerations dξ'/dt − rη' + qζ' etc.
results.modern_name: Equations of motion in a rotating frame (body-frame components; transport theorem)

results.what: Derivation of the antisymmetric angular-velocity quantities p, q, r from orthogonality of the direction cosines; ξ' = dξ/dt − rη + qζ etc.
results.modern_name: Ṙ Rᵀ is skew-symmetric (angular velocity tensor)

results.what: Velocity field of a Dirichlet ellipsoid expressed via two rotating frames (p, q, r and p1, q1, r1) and the axis rates, eq. (6)
results.modern_name: Riemann's two-frame description of Dirichlet–Dedekind–Riemann ellipsoids (precursor to the Riemann ellipsoid equations with u = (p+p1)/2, u' = (p−p1)/2)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of §1 of Riemann's published 1861 ellipsoid memoir; equations (3), (5) and (6) appear essentially verbatim in the printed paper. It has value only as a working draft.

checkable.sympy: t=symbols('t'); th,ph,ps=[Function(n)(t) for n in ('th','ph','ps')]; R=rot_axis3(ps)*rot_axis1(th)*rot_axis3(ph); W=simplify(R.diff(t)*R.T); simplify(W+W.T)==zeros(3)
checkable.asserts: For any rotation matrix R(t) whose rows are (α,β,γ),(α',β',γ'),(α'',β'',γ''), the matrix of sums Σ α_i α̇_j is antisymmetric. This underlies the definitions of p, q, r.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,p,q,r,p1,q1,r1,ad,bd,cd,X,Y,Z=symbols('a b c p q r p1 q1 r1 ad bd cd X Y Z'); xi,eta,zeta=a*X,b*Y,c*Z; dxi=ad*X+a*(r1*Y-q1*Z); deta=bd*Y+b*(-r1*X+p1*Z); dzeta=cd*Z+c*(q1*X-p1*Y); simplify(dxi-r*eta+q*zeta-(ad*X+(a*r1-b*r)*Y+(c*q-a*q1)*Z))==0
checkable.asserts: Inserting (5) (with X = ξ/a etc.) into (3) gives the first line of (6).
Second line of (6) has coefficient (b p1 − c p) for ζ/c (with the definitions from the previous check).
Third line of (6), unfinished on the page, follows from (3) and (5).

transcription_corrections: Eq. (5), first component: should read d(ξ/a)/dt = r1 η/b − q1 ζ/c, not '+ q1 ζ/c' (the sign is not clearly legible in the image; '−' is forced by the antisymmetry and by (6)).
Eq. (6), second line: the last coefficient is (b p1 − c p)·ζ/c, not '(cp1 − cp)'.

Opening line: 'Ersetzen wir nun in diesen Gleichungen statt der Coordinaten auch die Anfangswerthe der Grössen x, y, z, welche dort durch a, b, c bezeichnet' refers to Dirichlet's notation (initial coordinates a, b, c), which Riemann replaces by x0, y0, z0.
The quantities named p, q, r are the three mixed sums such as α'α̇+β'β̇+γ'γ̇. The displayed line 'α ∂α'/∂t + β ∂β'/∂t + γ ∂γ'/∂t = −…' is the antisymmetry relation, equal to −r.
